targetWords.definition: Access is the right to enter or use something.
targetWords.example: The manager was the only person with access to the password.

targetWords.definition: Conduct is the way that someone acts.
targetWords.example: • She was punished for her bad conduct.

targetWords.definition: When an event or action is constant, it happens a lot or all the time.
targetWords.example: The television at home is in constant use. crack [kraek] n.

targetWords.definition: -*■ The old window was covered with cracks.
targetWords.example: ■ The old window was covered with cracks. device [divais] n.

targetWords.definition: -* A thermometer is a device that tells temperature.
targetWords.example: A thermometer is a device that tells temperature.

targetWords.definition: To enclose something is to contain it.
targetWords.example: The cows in the field were enclosed by a fence.

targetWords.definition: To grip something is to hold it very tightly.
targetWords.example: I was scared, so I gripped my older sister's hand.

targetWords.definition: To halt is to stop moving.
targetWords.example: The criminal halted when he saw the police coming.

targetWords.definition: If something is impending, it is going to happen soon.
targetWords.example: ■ The student was nervous about his impending test.

targetWords.definition: To influence someone or something is to have an effect over them.
targetWords.example: • My friend influenced my decision to attend Terrance University. law [to:] n.

targetWords.definition: -> The students learned about different laws during social studies class.
targetWords.example: The students learned about different laws during social studies class. m ode [moud] n.

targetWords.definition: -* Mother turned the 7V to quiet mode while she talked on the phone.
targetWords.example: Mother turned the 7V to quiet mode while she talked on the phone.

targetWords.definition: To perspire means to sweat.
targetWords.example: I usually perspire a lot when I am at practice.

targetWords.definition: To replace something is to put it in the place of something else.
targetWords.example: I replaced the tire on my car because it was flat.

targetWords.definition: To snap something means to break it suddenly, which causes a loud noise.
targetWords.example: I took the stick and snapped it with my hands.

targetWords.definition: If a person or animal is sly, they are sneaky or good at tricking people.
targetWords.example: The sly fox stole the eggs from the nest.

targetWords.definition: To tend to do something is to be likely to do it or to do it often.
targetWords.example: My mom tends to buy me the perfect gift each Christmas.

targetWords.definition: When something is valid, it is correct or based on good reasoning.
targetWords.example: The expert's opinion on the subject was more valid than others. v e rsio n M>:/3an] n.

targetWords.definition: -* She read the students British version of the Chinese fairy tale.
targetWords.example: She read the students British version of the Chinese fairy tale.

targetWords.definition: You use whatsoever after a noun to emphasize that there is nothing of that thing.
targetWords.example: The boy had no idea whatsoever how to solve the story problem.

story.passage:
Janie had constant thoughts about getting a music player. One day, she was late to

class. She hurried down the hall but halted when she saw a backpack on the floor. She

looked inside and found nothing but some books. She reached inside the bag and felt a

small object at the bottom. It was a music player enclosed in a black case! Janie tended

to be honest, and she had no valid reason to take the device. However, her desire for

the player influenced her decision. Janie was being sly. She put the device into her own

backpack. When she arrived at class, she gave her teacher the bag. "I found this," she

said.

Ms. Johnson asked, "Does this backpack belong to anyone?" A girl named Linda

claimed the bag. Linda looked inside and yelled, "My music player

is missing! Janie took it!" Janie answered, "I did not." Linda

responded, "You were the only one that had access to it! If your

version of the story is true, you'll let Ms. Johnson check your bag."

Janie started to perspire as she realized the impending trouble

she was in. She gripped her bag tightly.

Ms. Johnson took the bag from Janie. Inside

she found the player. "Janie, I never expected

this kind of conduct from you," she said. "You've

always been such a good student."

Ms. Johnson gave Linda the player. Linda said, "Ms.

Johnson, look!" There was a crack along one side. She

turned it to the "on" mode, but it wouldn't work. It must've

snapped while Janie was holding onto the bag so tightly.

Ms. Johnson called Janie's parents. They were very upset.

"Stealing is illegal. You have no respect for the

law whatsoever," they said. "We bought you a

music player, but we're giving it to Linda. It

will replace the one you broke." In the end,

Janie's bad behavior left herwith nothing

at all.

_J
